title: Finite-subextension continuous cochains detect all cocycles and boundaries
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, a finite intermediate field $E$, a profinite group $G$ (compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected), and a finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space $W$ with jointly continuous $E$-linear $G$-action. For every finite intermediate $E\subseteq F\subseteq\Omega$, and for $F=\Omega$, put $V_F=F\otimes_E W$ with its finite product norm topology. The action is through $W$ and is trivial on $F$. All universes are as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Define $C^n_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,V_F)=C(G^n,V_F)$ for $n\geq0$, including $C^0_{\mathrm{cts}}=V_F$, with the differential
$$(df)(g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=g_1f(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{a=1}^n(-1)^af(g_1,\ldots,g_ag_{a+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(g_1,\ldots,g_n),$$
and $(dv)(g)=gv-v$ for $n=0$. This is the continuous cochain convention of [lem-sfb-continuous-cochain-finite-index-transfer]. Put $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{fin}}(G,V_\Omega)=\bigcup_{F\supseteq E}C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,V_F)$ inside $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,V_\Omega)$; each cochain must take all its values in one finite $V_F$. Both complexes vanish in negative degrees and have cohomology equal to kernel modulo image in abstract $E$-vector spaces, without closure of images [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

The actual inclusion $i:C^\bullet_{\mathrm{fin}}(G,V_\Omega)\hookrightarrow C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,V_\Omega)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. More explicitly, its map on $H^0$ is the identity on $V_\Omega^G$; for every $n\geq1$, a cocycle in $C^n_{\mathrm{fin}}$ which has a continuous $V_\Omega$-valued primitive has a primitive taking all its values in one finite $V_F$, and every continuous $V_\Omega$-valued $n$-cocycle is cohomologous to a cocycle taking all its values in one finite $V_F$. Thus $Q(i)$ is an isomorphism in the ordinary derived category $D(\mathbf{Ab})$. No bound on $n$, finite generation or cohomological dimension of $G$, completeness of $\Omega$, or discreteness of $W$ is assumed. This statement concerns explicit continuous cochains, without identifying them with internal condensed right derived invariants.

proof.text: Choose an $E$-basis of $W$ of size $d$, so the stipulated product topologies identify $V_L$ with $L^d$. Every action matrix has entries in $E$, hence the displayed differential preserves cochains with values in each $F^d$; inclusions commute with the differential. Two finite fields lie in their compositum, which is finite since its degree is at most the product of their degrees. Thus the union is a subcomplex. Every vector of $\Omega^d$ has finitely many algebraic coordinates, generating a finite extension of $E$. Consequently $C^0_{\mathrm{fin}}=V_\Omega=C^0_{\mathrm{cts}}$, and the degree-zero kernels are both $V_\Omega^G$. Both complexes vanish in negative degrees.

proof.text: Let $n\geq1$ and let $z\in C^n_{\mathrm{fin}}$ satisfy $dz=0$ and $z=db$ for a continuous $V_\Omega$-valued $(n-1)$-cochain $b$. Choose one finite $F\supseteq E$ containing every value of $z$. By [lem-sfb-finite-subfield-continuous-linear-retraction] there is a continuous $E$-linear retraction $p_F:\Omega\to F$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-scalar-cochain-retraction] with $L=\Omega$, this $p_F$, and the chosen coordinates. All field inclusions are continuous for the restricted absolute value, and the original $E^d$-action is jointly continuous by hypothesis. Its coordinate map $P$ is equivariant, continuous, fixes $F^d$ and satisfies $dP_*=P_*d$. Hence $d(P_*b)=P_*z=z$. This primitive takes all its values in that same finite $F^d$, proving injectivity of $H^n(i)$. This includes $n=1$, when $b$ is a single vector.

proof.text:
Let $n\geq1$ and $z\in Z^n_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,V_\Omega)$. By [lem-sfb-local-norm-algcl-cocycle-descent] choose an open $H\subseteq G$, finite $F\supseteq E$, cocycle $u\in C^n_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,V_F)$ and continuous $b$ with $\mathrm{res}(z)=ju+db$, where $j:V_F\hookrightarrow V_\Omega$. These are exactly its hypotheses and cochain convention. Compactness makes the disjoint open coset cover finite; write $m=[G:H]\geq1$. Apply [lem-sfb-continuous-cochain-finite-index-transfer] to both coefficient spaces, using its simultaneous naturality for the continuous equivariant inclusion $j$. Let $k$ be its homotopy, with $dk+kd=\mathrm{cor}_\Omega\mathrm{res}-m\,\mathrm{id}$ (negate a supplied homotopy if needed). Naturality gives $\mathrm{cor}_\Omega(ju)=j\mathrm{cor}_F(u)$. Since $dz=0$ and transfer is a cochain map,
$$m z=j\mathrm{cor}_F(u)+d(\mathrm{cor}_\Omega(b)-kz).$$
The field $E$ has characteristic zero, so $m^{-1}\in E$. Thus $v=m^{-1}\mathrm{cor}_F(u)$ is a continuous cocycle with all values in the one $V_F$, and
$$z-jv=d\bigl(m^{-1}(\mathrm{cor}_\Omega(b)-kz)\bigr).$$
This proves surjectivity of $H^n(i)$ without taking limits or closing images.

proof.text: Steps 1–3 show that every cohomology map of the actual inclusion is an isomorphism. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] this is a quasi-isomorphism, and localization sends it to an isomorphism $Q(i)$ in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$. The explicit primitive in step 2 and representative in step 3 give the asserted boundary and cocycle clauses. All computations concern the stated abstract kernel/image cohomology; no completeness, dimension bound on group cohomology or condensed derived-invariant comparison enters.
